title: MV Plugin to be able to create AI NPCs with Inworld API

posts.author: MIK0
posts.body:
Dear Makers of RPGs,
In light of the recent advancements in the gaming industry, driven by the AI revolution, I've been contemplating the possibility of creating a plugin to integrate the Inworld API into a text-input dialogue system for NPCs.
Have you all seen the astonishing demonstrations of the capabilities of Inworld's Origins? Several games, including Stardew Valley and Skyrim, have shown impressive implementations of this system. I urge you to see them for yourselves:
According to my research, numerous game development engines already support Inworld. Regrettably, RPG Maker isn't one of them, which is disappointing, to say the least
Nonetheless, I firmly believe that incorporating Inworld technology into RPG Maker holds immense potential. I'm hoping there might be someone among us with the necessary expertise to create an accessible build to turn this theoretical into a reality.
There have been incredible plugins that incorporated some level of chatbot technology, like
Llm-Chatbot by GiusTex
or
ChatGPT_APIMZ by Kotonoha
. But none has so far utilized Inworld's technology, which seems to be an excellent fit, particularly for creating AI NPCs.
I wonder if anyone in our community has the technical knowledge to build such a plugin. It could open up a whole new dimension of interactive and immersive storytelling for our RPG Maker projects.

That’s great to hear that you're potentially interested and willing to delve deeper into this
The primary difference I'm envisioning with Inworld API integration, as opposed to Llm-Chatbot or ChatGPT_APIMZ, is the remarkable intricacy and depth of contextual understanding it offers.
While Llm-Chatbot and ChatGPT_APIMZ do provide a level interactive element, Inworld API has demonstrated an exceptional ability to generate more lifelike and engaging dialogue. It brings forth the potential to create NPCs who can respond to player input in a far more nuanced and dynamic way.
Inworld technology seems to be designed strategically for AI NPC creation, which again, I believe could serve our RPG Maker games brilliantly. However, these are just my thoughts, and I would be interested to hear the community's ideas and feedback.

I do really enjoy typing to communicate with AI NPCs, and I believe I'm not alone. The act of typing out conversations creates a more intimate and active role playing experience that comes closer to the OG tabletop RPGs, allowing for greater player agency.
It deepens immersion by making characters respond uniquely to your input, improving emotional connections and enhancing replayability. It's also accessible for players who prefer or require a more measured pace of interaction. This human-AI interplay could well be the next frontier in evolving our digital adventures much like how storytelling evolves in a tabletop RPG, molding the narrative organically with each player interaction.
In my project for example, I envision crafting a super intelligent antagonist – a mastermind who isn't merely a roadblock for the hero but a complex character in their own right. The protagonist would have the option not just to fight this villain but to engage them in deep conversation, probing into the intricacies of their motives and gaining critical insights to influence the narrative's progression.
Envisioning this through the lens of Inworld AI's capabilities, we could develop an AI NPC that doesn't just regurgitate pre-written lines (like a cardboard cutout) but truly understands and interacts with the game's lore and context. This villain could argue persuasively, challenging the player to think critically about the story and the world they’re invested in. Every response from the AI would not only be unique but tailored to the dialogue's flow, making for a thoroughly convincing and dynamic character that can react logically and emotionally to the player's actions and choices.

I don't know if InWorld is a Large Language Model, but if it is a LLM, it does not process ideas "logically" or "emotionally", but generates words based on their statistical relationship with each other provided a given set of parameters. I bring this up because I think it's incredibly important to have a broad understanding of how generative AI like GPT or InWorld works so we have realistic expectations of what they can accomplish.

Fair point! I could’ve chosen words more carefully. You're quite right in your understanding of how generative AI models like GPT or InWorld's AI systems function. These are not sentient beings processing information logically or emotionally but rather complex algorithms predicting the next word in a sequence based on patterns they've learned from vast amounts of text data.
Their outputs are contingent upon the internal statistical modeling of language, and indeed, they lack genuine understanding or consciousness. However, despite these limitations, their ability to convincingly simulate conversation and generate contextually appropriate responses can be remarkably sophisticated.

Do as you please, nobody is forcing you to do so. It seems like you have a strong aversion to AI based on your previous posts and responses to discussions about it. However, I'm not entirely convinced that you fully undestand how one might apply AI in creating NPCs. Contrary to your belief, most developers, including myself, have no intention of using AI to replace the art of writing in a game. Even if some developers did, it would only lead to generic and predictable outcomes.
AI is simply a tool that we utilize to enhance interactive storytelling. It doesn't undermine the work of human writers. Just as writers use spelling checking algorithms to improve their work, creating AI NPCs allows us to account for the virtually limitless player input, resulting in a more personalized and realistic form of communication.
